claims.body: The Flames are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at keeping shots away. We’ll side with the Flames.

claims.head: McNabb and Theodore get the Backlund assignment
claims.call: The Golden Knights’ P1 (McNabb and Theodore) spends at least 55% of its 5-on-5 time against the Flames’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending McNabb and Theodore out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Flames’ first line is Backlund, Farabee and Sharangovich.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 6 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 47%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
S. Honzek is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Y. Sharangovich has taken his spot beside M. Backlund and J. Farabee.
J. Hanley has not dressed for the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. J. Middleton has taken his spot beside Z. Parekh.
J. Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
M. Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, up from 2% last season.
R. Andersson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, down from 48% last season.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights should be in control
VGK.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. If the Flames want to spoil it, start with piling up shots.

CGY.head: A steep climb for the Flames
CGY.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flames can still win it if they keep the shots coming, but a lot has to go their way.

story.head: Best against best
paras: The Flames come in at 1-5-0, the Golden Knights at 6-2-0.

It’s strength against strength: the Flames are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at keeping shots away. At home, Ryan Craig likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Flames’ first line.
